subject.title: [Feature]: deterministic context injection for bootstrap files and session-type filtering

question: Should OpenClaw expose a first-class bootstrap selector and dynamic command-expansion contract for sessions, and if so should command expansion be excluded, plugin-owned, or core-owned behind an explicit sandbox?
rationale: The remaining request changes public config/API behavior and adds possible command execution from bootstrap context, so automation cannot choose the long-term product and security boundary.

options.title: Narrow selector first
options.body: Add a small maintained bootstrap tier or selector contract and defer bootstrap command expansion until a separate security model is approved.

options.title: Plugin hook only
options.body: Route dynamic per-session context through documented hooks and keep core bootstrap loading limited to safe built-in files.

options.title: Full command expansion
options.body: Pursue bootstrap !command expansion only with explicit sandboxing, provenance, opt-in behavior, docs, and upgrade tests.

recommendation.title: Narrow selector first
recommendation.body: Add a small maintained bootstrap tier or selector contract and defer bootstrap command expansion until a separate security model is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for bootstrap resolution and session filtering points to steipete, and this choice needs product/API boundary ownership.
